title: streaming-lifecycle-controls: tighten client-cancel/disconnect handling and add reconnect/resume with server timeouts
author: Alicia Gomez
description: Motivation: streaming endpoints were brittle on client disconnects and customer infra reported stuck KV cache sessions and orphaned allocations when clients cancelled mid-stream. We also need a robust reconnect/resume flow compatible with the OpenAI-compat streaming semantics so long-lived clients can resume after transient network errors. This PR centralizes streaming lifecycle controls in the runtime, surfaces server-side timeouts, and extends the client-facing behavior to support reconnect/resume with token-accurate deduplication. Summary of changes: implemented explicit client-cancel propagation and server-side graceful shutdown of in-flight streams; added a reconnect token and resume window (configurable per model/route); introduced a reconnect manager that reconciles in-memory KV cache state and prevents double-emit on resume; added server-side streaming timeouts and backpressure signals to ensure resources are reclaimed for long-tail requests; updated SDK hooks (Python/TS) to expose reconnect tokens and automatic resume attempts; added OpenAI-compat mode adjustments for newline-delimited JSON streaming and function-calling boundary semantics. Backwards compatibility: old clients without reconnect tokens will continue to get deterministic cancellations and the server will fall back to per-request TTLs. Rollout plan: staged canary on Hosted API for 5% of traffic for 48 hours, followed by 25% then full rollout if no regressions. See tests and benchmarks below. Checklist: [x] implement runtime cancel propagation; [x] reconnect token API and storage; [x] SDK integrations (python/typescript); [x] unit and integration tests; [x] docs and migration notes; [x] canary rollout plan.
